decision2_theRefusalS3bPromisedIsNOTDeli.whatWasBuiltFirst: The first red suite committed in this session DID assert `{kind:'blocked', reason:'recovery-fact-read-failed'}` for an admitted, create-path-seeded match whose capability database is closed, discriminated on the presence of `mp_journal_authority_baseline` (a write-once MATCH-database row, therefore readable exactly when the effective head is not).
decision2_theRefusalS3bPromisedIsNOTDeli.whyItWasWithdrawn: MEASURED, not argued. `DurableMatchStore.mirrorCommittedBatch` opens with `if (!this.isCapabilityDbAvailable()) return;` (DurableMatchStore.ts:1003), so a match can be ADMITTED at mode 'enabled' (journalAuthorityAdmission.ts `resolveJournalAuthorityForNewMatch` inserts the baseline) and never mirror a single row. Admission and mirroring therefore diverge in exactly the process state that makes the head unreadable, and the admission baseline cannot discriminate them. Mutant M2 of slice 1 is the direct measurement: implementing the baseline-keyed refusal kills `journal-authority rollback proof > proves baseline-only rollback compares every persisted baseline tuple field to the durable head`, a row whose whole subject is that such a match still serves legacy and still commits. Refusing there would contradict task 1.7's own text, "legacy completed matches keep their reads". Log: s7b1-mutant-M2.log.
decision2_theRefusalS3bPromisedIsNOTDeli.whatWasShippedInstead: `unavailable` continues to read as no head, and that answer is now PINNED by a row named for the fact that S7-d must turn it red: `still selects the legacy reader for an admitted match whose head is unreadable` in matchMarkerRetirementRecovery.sqlite.test.ts. The S3-b tripwire row was rewritten to assert the legacy answer with a comment saying the refusal was not decidable here and why.
decision2_theRefusalS3bPromisedIsNOTDeli.whatWouldMakeItDecidable: A durable, capability-db-independent per-match record of whether the stream was ever MIRRORED. That is S7-d's migration state (the combat analog of CampaignAuthorityMigrationState). Building it here was out of scope by charter (no migrations, S7-d untouched) and would have collided with S7-d's own ownership.
decision2_theRefusalS3bPromisedIsNOTDeli.ownerVisibility: Carried as open question OQ-1 below. This is the one place where what shipped is narrower than the S5-S7 brief's literal S7-b redFirstTest.

decision3_theWriteGoesWithTheReads.what: commitJournalAuthorityCommand no longer builds an IMatchJournalAuthorityStarted nor sets `journalAuthorityStarted` on the batch, and the `alreadyStarted` read that existed only to keep that write to once is gone with it.
decision3_theWriteGoesWithTheReads.whyNotJustLeaveIt: A durable write-once row on the match database that looks exactly like an answer to "has this stream started" is the second source task 1.3 exists to remove; leaving the writer would keep minting new ones. `commitJournalAuthorityCommand` throws unless `journal.enabled`, and admission requires mode 'enabled' (journalAuthorityAdmission.ts `admitJournalAuthority`: `if (input.mode !== 'enabled' || !input.requested) return {kind:'inert'}`), so the write is unreachable at the shipped mode and its removal cannot change production behaviour today.
decision3_theWriteGoesWithTheReads.measuredReach: After S7-a2's create-path seeding the write was ALREADY skipped for every capability-backed match (the derived head answers 'started' on the first command). Its remaining reach was exactly the stores with no journal behind them — InMemoryMatchStore, and DurableMatchStore with no capability database — which is where a marker asserting 'started' is least defensible. s7b2-red.log measures this: the durable row passed before the change; only the two in-memory rows were red.
decision3_theWriteGoesWithTheReads.behaviouralNarrowingAtNonOffModes_F2: NAMED AFTER REVIEW (finding F2), and re-verified independently in this session. Removing the `alreadyStarted` read also removed its try/catch, which typed a thrown EventHistoryBranchError('branch-integrity') from a corrupt persisted head into a fail-closed `persistenceFailure(..., 'started read failed')` on the COMMAND path (b9ab4a668:src/lib/multiplayer/server/ServerMatchHostJournalAuthority.ts lines 199-210, removed at HEAD; `git grep 'started read failed' dd6c5e7bf -- src/` now returns nothing). At HEAD the command path never touches the head, so at mode 'enabled' a match with a corrupt persisted head COMMITS its command and the mirror's own catch records a `journal-mirror:<reason>` shadow mismatch (DurableMatchStore.mirrorCommittedBatch) instead of refusing typed. INERT AT THE SHIPPED MODE: at mode 'off' nothing mirrors and the head is never consulted on the command path at all, so there is no behaviour to narrow. UNPINNED AT BASE: no test fell when the catch went, which is why the blast-radius measurement did not surface it — the only 'corrupt head' rows are derivation and recovery rows (journalAuthorityStartedDerived.sqlite.test.ts, matchRecoveryStartedFromJournalHead.sqlite.test.ts), and recovery's typed refusal plus S4's divergence refusal still catch the shape at boot. This corrects decision3's earlier wording, which said only that the removal 'cannot change production behaviour today' — true for mode 'off', but not the whole story. Carried as S7b-Q6.

openQuestions.title: The `unavailable` refusal S3-b promised is deferred to S7-d, not delivered here
openQuestions.detail: S3-b's row 1 and the S5-S7 brief both name 'unavailable + marker -> blocked' as S7-b's headline. It is not deliverable without a durable, capability-db-independent record that a stream was MIRRORED; the admission baseline records ADMISSION, and mutant M2 measures that refusing on it breaks the shipped `baseline-only` legacy read. Today's answer (legacy reader) is pinned by the row `still selects the legacy reader for an admitted match whose head is unreadable`, written so S7-d turns it red deliberately.
openQuestions.askOfTheOwner: Confirm that the refusal moves to S7-d's per-match migration state, and that S7-b's receipt narrowing the brief's redFirstTest is accepted.

openQuestions.title: The wording-amendment ruling is still owed: does the table, the read port and the batch field go?
openQuestions.detail: The S5-S7 brief flags this as an owner ruling and recommends dropping the write, the read AND the table. This session delivered the production write and both production reads; the mechanism remains. Recommendation unchanged: drop all three, since the derived head is now the only thing production consults and a shim would recreate the two-sources drift task 1.3 exists to remove. The table can be retired non-destructively by removing its `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` (new databases stop carrying it; existing rows are never erased, which matches the rollback law's 'no row erased').

openQuestions.title: A create-path-seeded match with no committed command recovers as blocked/'missing-journal-head'
openQuestions.detail: Measured while writing slice 1's suite, not previously recorded: after S7-a2, a match seeded on create has an effective head but no command receipt, so `journalHeadFromReceipt` returns null and `selectMatchRollbackReader` blocks with 'missing-journal-head'. openQuestions.detail: See the F2 section for the mechanism, file:line and the inert-at-mode-off statement. In one line: at mode 'enabled' a corrupt persisted head no longer refuses a command typed; it commits and records a shadow mismatch. Inert at the shipped mode, unpinned at base, disclosed on the PR.

Either way it wants a pinning row; there is none today.

F2.title: Removing the alreadyStarted read also removed the command path's fail-closed catch for a corrupt persisted head
F2.source: Review finding F2 (severity low-medium, non-blocking). Reproduced independently in this session rather than taken on the reviewer's word.
F2.mechanism: At base, commitJournalAuthorityCommand wrapped the alreadyStarted read in a try/catch whose sole purpose, per its own comment, was: a corrupt head throws here, between this function's two try blocks, so it is caught and typed into the same fail-closed STORE_FAILURE shape the store's own append failures take, rather than escaping the command path uncaught. deriveMatchJournalAuthorityStartedHead deliberately does NOT catch EventHistoryBranchError branch-integrity: a head naming a non-effective branch is persisted corruption and the derivation lets it throw. Removing the read removed the catch with it, so the command path no longer consults head integrity at all.
F2.fileLine: src/lib/multiplayer/server/ServerMatchHostJournalAuthority.ts, b9ab4a668 lines 199-210 (the let alreadyStarted / try / catch block returning persistenceFailure with reason 'started read failed'). Removed by fd76b3dc1. Verified absent at HEAD: git grep 'started read failed' dd6c5e7bf -- src/ returns nothing.
F2.behaviourAtModeEnabled: A match whose persisted effective head names a non-effective branch used to have its next command refused typed. It now COMMITS that command, and the corruption surfaces only as a journal-mirror shadow mismatch recorded by DurableMatchStore.mirrorCommittedBatch's own catch: a counter, not a refusal.
F2.inertAtModeOff: STATED EXPLICITLY: at the shipped mode COMBAT_JOURNAL_AUTHORITY_MODE = 'off' (matchJournalAuthority.ts:18-19, re-read at HEAD) this path is unreachable twice over. commitJournalAuthorityCommand throws unless journal.enabled, and admission requires mode 'enabled' (admitJournalAuthority returns inert unless mode is 'enabled' and the match requested it). There is no production behaviour to narrow.
F2.unpinnedAtBase: No test fell when the catch was removed. The 10 failures the blast-radius run measured were all marker-arm rows. The only corrupt-head rows in the tree are a derivation row (journalAuthorityStartedDerived.sqlite.test.ts) and a recovery row (matchRecoveryStartedFromJournalHead.sqlite.test.ts); neither drives the command path. That is why the measurement did not surface it, and it is the honest reason this was found by review rather than by the slice.
F2.whyItIsStillDefensible: The guard existed only for a read that no longer happens; keeping it would have meant keeping the read, which is the thing task 1.3 retires. Recovery's typed refusal and S4's divergence refusal still catch the corrupt-head shape at boot, so a corrupt stream is still refused before it is served, just not mid-command.
F2.correctsTheReceipt: design.decision3 previously said only that the removal cannot change production behaviour today. True at mode 'off', but not the whole story, and the unqualified phrasing understated a real narrowing at mode 'enabled'.
F2.carriedAs: S7b-Q6 (see openQuestions), a question for S7-d: should the command path consult head integrity at all, or is boot-time refusal the intended boundary?
